In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Indeed, the convulsion of the Hour is a tremendous thing [[The words between the brackets are an addition from manuscript "ب".]] on the Day you see it, every nursing mother will forget what she was nursing, every pregnant woman will drop her load, and you will see people intoxicated, but they will not be intoxicated; rather, the punishment of Allah is severe.﴾ (2)

﴿O mankind, fear your Lord﴾ means: beware of His punishment by obeying Him. ﴿Indeed, the convulsion of the Hour is a tremendous thing﴾. Al-zalzalah and al-zilzal mean an intense shaking in a terrifying state. The scholars differed concerning this convulsion:

Alqamah and al-Sha'bi said: it is one of the signs of the Hour. [It was also said: it is the establishment of the Hour.]

Al-Hasan and al-Suddi said: this convulsion will occur on the Day of Resurrection.

Ibn Abbas said: the convulsion of the Hour is its establishment, so it will be with it.

﴿On the Day you see it﴾ means the Hour. It was also said: the convulsion. ﴿Will forget﴾: Ibn Abbas said: will be occupied (distracted). It was also said: will forget. It is said: "dhahaltu 'an kadha," meaning I left it and became occupied with something else.

﴿Every nursing mother will forget what she was nursing﴾ means: every woman who has a child she is nursing. It is said "imra'ah murdi'" without a ta' when it is used as a description, like "ha'id" and "hamil." When they intend the verb, they add the ta' (as in "murdi'ah").

﴿And every pregnant woman will drop her load﴾ means: she will miscarry her child because of the terror of that Day.

Al-Hasan said: the nursing mother will be distracted from her child without weaning, and the pregnant woman will drop what is in her womb prematurely. [Reported by al-Tabari: 17/114.] This indicates that this convulsion occurs in this world, because after resurrection there is no pregnancy.

Whoever says it occurs on the Day of Resurrection says this to magnify the matter, not in its literal sense, like their saying: "A matter befell us in which the newborn turns gray," meaning its severity.

﴿And you see people intoxicated, but they are not intoxicated﴾. Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read "sakra wa-ma hum bi-sakra" without the alif. Both are dialectal forms for the plural of "sakran," like "kasla" and "kusala."

Al-Hasan said: the meaning is: you see people intoxicated from fear, but they are not intoxicated from wine.

It was also said: the meaning is: you see people as though they were intoxicated. ﴿But the punishment of Allah is severe.﴾

Al-Imam Abu Ali al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Qadi informed us; Abu Tahir Muhammad ibn Mahmash al-Ziyadi informed us; Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Umar ibn Hafs al-Tajir informed us; Ibrahim ibn Abdullah ibn Umar ibn Bukayr al-Kufi al-Absi informed us; Waki' informed us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Salih, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will say on the Day of Resurrection: O Adam, stand up and send forth the group for the Fire. He will say: Here I am, at Your service and pleasure, and all good is in Your hands. O Lord, what is the group for the Fire? He will say: From every thousand, nine hundred and ninety-nine. Then the newborn will turn gray, and every pregnant woman will drop her load, and you will see people intoxicated, but they will not be intoxicated; rather, the punishment of Allah is severe." They will say: "And which of us is that one?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Nine hundred and nine hundred and ninety from Gog and Magog, and one from you." The people said: "Allahu akbar!" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "By Allah, I hope that you will be a quarter of the people of Paradise. By Allah, I hope that you will be a third of the people of Paradise. By Allah, I hope that you will be half of the people of Paradise." He said: The people exclaimed "Allahu akbar." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "On that Day you will be among the people no more than a white hair on a black ox, or a black hair on a white ox." It is also narrated from Imran ibn Husayn, Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, and others, that these two verses were revealed during the expedition of Banu al-Mustaliq, at night. The herald of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) called out, so they urged their mounts until they gathered around the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he recited them to them. Then no one was seen weeping more than they did that night. When they awoke in the morning, they did not unsaddle their mounts, did not pitch their tents, and did not cook any pot, while the people were between weeping, sitting sorrowful and reflecting. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Do you know what day that is?" They said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said: "That is the Day when Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will say to Adam: stand up and send forth the group for the Fire from your offspring. Adam will say: From how many? Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will say: From every thousand, nine hundred and ninety-nine to the Fire, and one to Paradise." He said: This was hard upon the Muslims, and they wept and said: "Then who will be saved, O Messenger of Allah?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Rejoice, be upright, and seek to be near the mark, for among you are two creatures that have never been among a people without multiplying them: Gog and Magog." Then he said: "Indeed, I hope that you will be a third of the people of Paradise." They exclaimed "Allahu akbar" and praised Allah. Then he said: "Indeed, I hope that you will be half of the people of Paradise." They exclaimed "Allahu akbar" and praised Allah. Then he said: "Indeed, I hope that you will be two-thirds of the people of Paradise. The people of Paradise are one hundred and twenty rows, eighty of which are my community. The Muslims among the disbelievers are only like a mole on the side of a camel, or like a spot on the foreleg of a beast; rather, like a black hair on a white ox, or a white hair on a black ox." Then he said: "And seventy thousand of my community will enter Paradise without reckoning." Umar said: "Seventy thousand?" He said: "Yes, and with each one, seventy thousand." Then Ukkashah ibn Mihsan stood up and said: "O Messenger of Allah, pray to Allah that He makes me one of them." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "You are one of them." Then a man from the Ansar stood up and said: "Pray to Allah that He makes me one of them." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Ukkashah has preceded you with it." [Reported by al-Tirmidhi 9/12-13, up to his saying "in the foreleg of a beast," and he said: this is a hasan sahih hadith; and Imam Ahmad 4/435, up to his saying "or a spot on the foreleg of a beast"; and al-Hakim 2/385, who said: this hadith has a sound chain but they (al-Bukhari and Muslim) did not include it; and Ibn Hajar attributed it in al-Kafi al-Shafi p. 112 to al-Tha'labi and al-Baghawi, then said: as for its end, I have not seen it.]

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 22, verse 12–13:

﴿He calls upon, besides Allah, that which does not harm him﴾ if he disobeys it and does not worship it, ﴿and that which does not benefit him﴾ if he obeys it and worships it. ﴿That is the far-straying error﴾ from the truth and right guidance.

﴿He calls upon one whose harm is closer than his benefit﴾. This verse is among the difficult verses of the Qur'an, and there are questions concerning it:

The first of them: They said: Allah has said in the first verse, "He calls upon, besides Allah, that which does not harm him," and He says here, "one whose harm is closer." So how can these two be reconciled?

It was said: His saying in the first verse, "He calls upon, besides Allah, that which does not harm him," means that abandoning its worship does not harm it. And His saying, ﴿whose harm is closer﴾, means the harm of worshipping it.

If it is said: He has said, "one whose harm is closer than his benefit," yet there is no benefit at all in worshipping an idol?

It is said: This is according to the custom of the Arabs, for they say of what does not exist at all that it is "far away." Like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿That is a far-off return﴾ (Qaf 50:3), meaning there is no return at all. So, since the benefit of the idol is far away, in the sense that there is no benefit in it at all, it was said: "its harm is closer," because it is actual.

The third question: His saying ﴿whose harm is closer﴾, what is the purpose of this lam (ل)? They differed concerning it. Some of them said: it is a supplementary (ṣilah) lam, its meaning being: "He calls upon whose harm is closer." Thus Ibn Mas'ud also recited it. It was also said: "li-man darruhu" means "to the one whose harm is closer than his benefit." It was also said: "yad'u" is in the sense of "yaqulu" (says), and the predicate is omitted, meaning: he says, "for one whose harm is closer than his benefit, he is a god."

It was also said: its meaning is, "He calls upon, for one whose harm is closer than his benefit, He calls upon," so the last "yad'u" is omitted, being sufficed by the first. If you say, "He strikes for one whose good is more than his evil, he strikes," then omitting the last is permissible.

It was also said: it is for emphasis, its meaning being: "He calls upon, by Allah, one whose harm is closer than his benefit."

It was also said: "yad'u man" is a continuation of His saying, "That is the far-straying error." He says: "That is the far-straying error, he calls upon," then he resumes and says, "one whose harm is closer than his benefit," so "man" is in the nominative position as the subject of a nominal sentence, and its predicate is: ﴿Surely evil is the patron﴾, that is, the helper. It was also said: the one worshipped.

﴿And surely evil is the companion﴾, that is, the associate and the one who mixes closely, meaning: the idol. The Arabs call a spouse "ʿashīr" (companion) because of the close association.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 22, verse 14–15:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, Allah will admit those who have believed and done righteous deeds into gardens beneath which rivers flow. Indeed, Allah does whatever He wills.﴾

﴿Whoever should think that Allah will never support him⦆ — meaning His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ — ﴿in this world and the Hereafter, let him extend a rope⦆ — a cord ﴿to the sky⦆. By "the sky" is meant the roof of the house, according to the view of the majority, that is: let him tie a rope to the roof of his house and hang himself with it until he dies. ﴿Then let him cut it off⦆ — the rope — after the strangulation. It is also said: "Then let him cut it off" means: let him stretch the rope until it snaps, so that he dies strangled. ﴿Then let him look: will his scheme remove⦆ — his device and his stratagem — ﴿that which enrages him?⦆ "Mā" here is in the sense of a verbal noun: will his scheme and his stratagem remove his rage? Its meaning: let him choke with rage until he dies. This is not meant as a binding command, that he should actually do it, since it is not possible for him to cut and look after being strangled and dead; rather, it is as one says to an envious person: "If you are not pleased with this, then choke yourself and die of rage."

Ibn Zayd said: the intended "sky" is the well-known sky.

The meaning of the verse: whoever thinks that Allah will not support His Prophet and that he can plot against his affair in order to cut it off from him, let him cut it off at its root, for its root is from the sky. Let him extend a rope to the sky, then let him cut off from the Prophet ﷺ the revelation that comes to him, and then let him look whether he is able, by this act, to remove his rage.

It is narrated that this verse was revealed concerning a people from Asad and Ghatafan whom the Prophet ﷺ had invited to Islam. There was an alliance between them and the Jews, and they said: "We cannot become Muslims, for we fear that Muhammad will not be supported and that his affair will not prevail, so the alliance between us and the Jews will be severed, and they will not supply us with provisions nor shelter us." So this verse was revealed. [[Mentioned by al-Tabari: 17/128, without a chain.]]

Mujahid said: "al-nasr" (support) here means provision (rizq), and the pronoun refers back to ﴿man⦆ (whoever). Its meaning: whoever thinks that Allah will not provide for him in this world and the Hereafter. It was revealed concerning one who thought ill of Allah, the Exalted, and feared that Allah would not provide for him: "let him extend a rope to the sky," that is, to the sky of the house, then let him look whether that act of his removes what enrages him, namely the fear of not being provided for.

Support (nasr) may also come to mean provision. The Arabs say: "Whoever gives me support, may Allah support him," meaning: whoever gives me, may Allah give him. Abu Ubayda said: the Arabs say "a land that is manṣūrah," meaning "rained upon."

Abu 'Amr, Nafi', Ibn 'Amir and Ya'qub read "thumma liyaqta' " and "thumma liyaqḍū" with a kasra on the lam, while the rest read them with a sukun, since in all cases it is the lam of command. Ibn 'Amir additionally read ﴿wa-liyūfū nudhūrahum wa-liyattawwafū⦆ (al-Hajj: 29) with a kasra on the lam in both places. Whoever read with a kasra in "thumma liyaqta'" and in "thumma liyaqḍū" differentiated on the basis that "thumma" is separated from the speech, while the waw seems to be part of the same word, like the fa' in His saying "fa-liyanzur."

Mujahid said: "al-nasr" (support) here means provision (rizq), and the pronoun refers back to ﴿man⦆ (whoever). Its meaning: whoever thinks that Allah will not provide for him in this world and the Hereafter. It was revealed concerning one who thought ill of Allah, the Exalted, and feared that Allah would not provide for him: "let him extend a rope to the sky," that is, to the sky of the house, then let him look whether that act of his removes what enrages him, namely the fear of not being provided for.

Support (nasr) may also come to mean provision. The Arabs say: "Whoever gives me support, may Allah support him," meaning: whoever gives me, may Allah give him. Abu Ubayda said: the Arabs say "a land that is manṣūrah," meaning "rained upon."

Abu 'Amr, Nafi', Ibn 'Amir and Ya'qub read "thumma liyaqta' " and "thumma liyaqḍū" with a kasra on the lam, while the rest read them with a sukun, since in all cases it is the lam of command. Ibn 'Amir additionally read ﴿wa-liyūfū nudhūrahum wa-liyattawwafū⦆ (al-Hajj: 29) with a kasra on the lam in both places. Whoever read with a kasra in "thumma liyaqta'" and in "thumma liyaqḍū" differentiated on the basis that "thumma" is separated from the speech, while the waw seems to be part of the same word, like the fa' in His saying "fa-liyanzur."

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 22, verses 16–18:

﴿And thus﴾, i.e., in the same way, meaning what has preceded of the verses of the Qur'an, ﴿We have sent it down﴾, meaning the Qur'an, ﴿as clear signs, and that Allah guides whom He wills﴾. ﴿Indeed, those who believe, and those who are Jews, and the Sabians, and the Christians, and the Magians, and those who associate others with Allah﴾, meaning the worshippers of idols, ﴿indeed Allah will judge between them﴾, i.e., He will decide between them, ﴿on the Day of Resurrection. Indeed Allah is Witness over all things﴾. ﴿Have you not seen﴾, i.e., have you not known; and it is said: ﴿Have you not seen﴾ [read] [[addition from "b".]] with your heart ﴿that to Allah prostrate whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth, and the sun and the moon and the stars and the mountains and the trees and the moving creatures﴾.

Mujahid said: Their prostration is the shifting of their shadows. Abu al-'Aliyah said: There is no star, nor sun, nor moon in the sky except that it falls prostrate when it sets, then it does not turn back until it is given permission, so it takes the right-hand course until it returns to its place of rising. It is also said: Their prostration means obedience, for there is no inanimate thing except that it is obedient to Allah, humbled before Him, and glorifying Him, as Allah the Exalted informed concerning the heavens and the earth: ﴿They said, "We came willingly"﴾ (Fussilat: 11), and He said about the description of stones: ﴿And indeed, among them is that which descends out of fear of Allah﴾ (al-Baqarah: 74), and the Exalted said: ﴿And there is not a thing but that it exalts [Allah] by His praise, but you do not understand their glorification﴾ (al-Isra': 44). This is a good view, consistent with the position of the People of the Sunnah.

As for His saying: ﴿And many among mankind﴾, i.e., of all these things, they glorify Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, "and many among mankind", meaning the Muslims.

﴿And many deserve the punishment﴾, and these are the disbelievers, because of their disbelief and their abandoning of prostration, and despite their disbelief, their shadows prostrate to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. The waw in His saying: ﴿And many deserve the punishment﴾ is the waw of resumption (isti'naf).

﴿And whoever Allah humiliates﴾, i.e., Allah humiliates him, ﴿for him there is no honorer﴾, i.e., whomever Allah humiliates, no one honors him. ﴿Indeed, Allah does what He wills﴾, i.e., He honors and humiliates; so happiness and wretchedness are by His will and His decree.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 22, verse 19:

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿These two adversaries dispute concerning their Lord﴾, meaning: they argued about His religion and His command. The word khasm (adversary, opponent) is a noun resembling a verbal noun (ism shabih bil-masdar), which is why He said ﴿dispute﴾ in the plural form, as in His saying: ﴿And has the news of the adversaries reached you, when they climbed over the wall of the prayer chamber?﴾ (Sad 38:21). They differed concerning these two adversaries:

ʿAbd al-Wahid al-Maliḥi informed us, Ahmad ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Nuʿaymi informed us, Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us, Yaʿqub ibn Ibrahim informed us, Hushaym informed us, Abu Hashim informed us, from Abu Mijlaz, from Qays ibn ʿAbbad, who said: I heard Abu Dharr swear an oath that this verse, ﴿These two adversaries dispute concerning their Lord﴾, was revealed concerning those who came forth on the day of Badr: Hamzah and ʿAli, ʿUbaydah ibn al-Harith, ʿUtbah and Shaybah, the two sons of Rabiʿah, and al-Walid ibn ʿUtbah. [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Maghazi, chapter on the killing of Abu Jahl: 7/297, and Muslim in al-Tafsir, chapter on His saying (These two adversaries dispute concerning their Lord), no. (3033), 4/2323.]]

And ʿAbd al-Wahid al-Maliḥi informed us, Ahmad al-Nuʿaymi informed us, Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us, Hajjaj ibn Minhal informed us, al-Muʿtamir ibn Sulayman narrated to us, who said: I heard my father say: Abu Mijlaz informed us, from Qays ibn ʿAbbad, from ʿAli ibn Abi Talib, who said: I will be the first to kneel before the Most Merciful for litigation on the Day of Resurrection. Qays said: And concerning them this verse was revealed: ﴿These two adversaries dispute concerning their Lord﴾. He said: They are those who came forth on the day of Badr: ʿAli and Hamzah, ʿUbaydah, Shaybah ibn Rabiʿah, and ʿUtbah ibn Rabiʿah, and al-Walid ibn ʿUtbah. [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Maghazi, chapter on the killing of Abu Jahl: 7/296.]]

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: On the day of Badr, ʿUtbah ibn Rabiʿah came out between his brother Shaybah ibn Rabiʿah and his son al-Walid ibn ʿUtbah, and called for single combat. Young men of the Ansar came out to him, three of them: ʿAwdh and Muʿawwidh, the sons of al-Harith, whose mother was ʿAfra', and ʿAbd Allah ibn Rawahah. They said: Who are you? They said: A group of the Ansar. They said, when they had identified themselves: "You are equals, noble ones." Then their herald called out: "O Muhammad, bring out to us our equals from among our people." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Stand up, O ʿUbaydah ibn al-Harith, O Hamzah ibn ʿAbd al-Muttalib, and O ʿAli ibn Abi Talib." When they drew near, they said: "Who are you?" They named themselves and said: "Yes, you are equals, noble ones." ʿUbaydah fought against ʿUtbah, who was the eldest of the group; Hamzah fought against Shaybah; and ʿAli fought against al-Walid ibn ʿUtbah. Hamzah did not delay in killing Shaybah, and ʿAli killed al-Walid. ʿUbaydah and ʿUtbah exchanged two blows, each of which wounded the other. Then Hamzah and ʿAli turned with their swords upon ʿUtbah and finished him off, and they carried ʿUbaydah back to his companions, his leg severed and its marrow flowing. When they brought ʿUbaydah to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), he said: "Am I not a martyr, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Yes." ʿUbaydah said: "If Abu Talib were alive, he would know that we are more deserving of what he said," where he says: "We surrender him until we are struck down around him, and we forget our sons and our wives." [[See: al-Sirah al-Nabawiyyah of Ibn Hisham with al-Rawd al-Unf: 2/67–68.]]

Ibn ʿAbbas and Qatadah said: The verse was revealed concerning the Muslims and the People of the Book. The People of the Book said: "We are closer to God and older in scripture than you, and our Prophet came before your Prophet." The believers said: "We are more deserving of God. We believed in our Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) and your Prophet and in what God has sent down of scripture, while you know our Prophet and our scripture and you disbelieved in it out of envy." This is their dispute concerning their Lord. [[Narrated by al-Tabari: 17/132, from Ibn ʿAbbas.]]

Mujahid, ʿAta' ibn Abi Rabah and al-Kalbi said: They are the believers and the disbelievers, all of them, of whatever religion they were.[[See al-Tabari: 17/132.]]

Some of them said: He made the religions six in His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, those who believed and those who were Jews﴾ (al-Ma'idah 5:69), and so on, making five for the Fire and one for the Garden. So His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿These two adversaries dispute concerning their Lord﴾ refers to them: the believers are one adversary, and the remaining five are the other adversary.

ʿIkrimah said: They are the Garden and the Fire, which disputed, as Hassan ibn Saʿid al-Mani'i informed us, Abu Tahir al-Ziyadi informed us, Abu Bakr Muhammad Husayn al-Qattan informed us, Ahmad ibn Yusuf al-Sulami informed us, ʿAbd al-Razzaq informed us, Maʿmar informed us, from Hammam ibn Munabbih, who said: Abu Hurayrah narrated to us, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The Garden and the Fire disputed. The Fire said: 'I have been given preference over the arrogant and the tyrants.' The Garden said: 'What is wrong with me that only the weak among people enter me, and their lowly ones and their deluded ones?' Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said to the Garden: 'You are My mercy; I show mercy through you to whomever I will of My servants.' And He said to the Fire: 'You are My punishment; I punish through you whomever I will of My servants. Each of you will have its fill. As for the Fire, it will not be filled until Allah places His foot in it, and it says: "Enough, enough," and then it is filled and its parts draw together, and Allah does not wrong any of His creatures. As for the Garden, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will create for it a creation.'" [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Tafsir, chapter on (and it says: Is there any more?) 8/595; Muslim in Paradise and its Bliss, chapter: The Fire is entered by the tyrants and the Garden is entered by the weak, no. (2846) 4/2186; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 15/256–257.]] Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, explained what awaits the two adversaries, saying:

﴿So those who disbelieve, garments of fire will be cut out for them﴾. Saʿid ibn Jubayr said: "Garments of molten brass. Nothing among vessels, when heated, is more intensely hot than it, and it was named with the name of garments because it encompasses them as garments encompass a person."

Some of them said: The people of the Fire will wear cut-up pieces of fire. ﴿Boiling water will be poured over their heads﴾. Al-hamim (boiling water) is hot water whose heat has reached its utmost.

﴿Whereby there will be melted﴾, i.e., melted by the boiling water (al-hamim), ﴿what is in their bellies﴾. It is said: "I melted the rump-fat and the fat with fire" when you melt them; the verb is ṣahartu (ṣahr), with the present aṣharu. The meaning is that what is in their bellies is melted by the boiling water which is poured down over their heads, until the fats and the entrails in their bellies fall away, ﴿and the skins﴾, i.e., its heat scorches their skins so that they are peeled off.

We were informed by Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Abi Tawbah; we were informed by Abu Tahir Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn al-Harith; we were informed by Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn Ya'qub al-Kisa'i; we were informed by Abdullah ibn Mahmud; we were informed by Ibrahim ibn Abdullah al-Khallal; we were informed by Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak, from Sa'id ibn Zayd, from Abu al-Samh, from Abu Juhayrah, whose name is Abd al-Rahman, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Indeed the boiling water is poured over their heads, and it penetrates the skull until it reaches their interior, and it dissolves what is in their interior until it exits from their feet. This is the ṣahr. Then they are restored as they were." [Narrated by al-Tirmidhi in the chapter on the description of the people of Hell, the chapter on what has been related about the description of the drink of the people of the Fire, 7/302-303, and he said: "This is a gharib ṣahih hadith." Also by Imam Ahmad, 2/374; al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak, 2/387; al-Tabari, 17/133-134; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah, 15/244. al-Albani weakened its chain in his commentary on al-Mishkat, 3/1581.]

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 22, verses 21–23:

Allah's words: ﴿And for them are hooked rods of iron.﴾ These are whips of iron. Its singular is miqma'ah (a hooked rod). Al-Layth said: al-miqma'ah is like a mace of iron, from their saying "qama'tu ra'sahu" (I struck his head), when you strike it with a violent blow. And in a report: "If a hooked rod of iron were placed in the earth and then the two weighty ones (mankind and jinn) gathered together to lift it from the earth, they would not be able to lift it." [[Narrated by al-Hakim: 4/600, through the transmission of Darraj, from Abu al-Haytham, and by Imam Ahmad: 3/29. Al-Haythami said in Majma' al-Zawa'id (10/388): "Ahmad and Abu Ya'la narrated it, and in its chain are weak narrators who were deemed trustworthy." See also al-Kafi al-Shaf, p. 112, and al-Targhib wa'l-Tarhib: 4/474.]]

﴿Every time they wish to get out of it, from distress﴾ That is: every time they attempt to leave the Fire, because of the distress and anguish that overtakes them and seizes their breath. ﴿they are returned into it﴾ That is: they are driven back into it with the hooked rods. And in the tafsir: Hell will surge with them, casting them up to its top, and they will wish to exit it, but the angels of punishment will strike them with hooked rods of iron, and they will fall back into it for seventy autumns.

﴿And taste the punishment of the burning.﴾ That is: the angels will say to them, "Taste the punishment of the burning," meaning the burning one, like "al-alim" (painful) and "al-wajia" (grievous).

Al-Zajjaj said: These are one of the two adversaries. And He said about the other, who are the believers: ﴿Indeed, Allah will admit those who believe and do righteous deeds into gardens beneath which rivers flow; they will be adorned therein with bracelets of gold﴾ ﴿Indeed, Allah will admit those who believe and do righteous deeds into gardens beneath which rivers flow; they will be adorned therein with bracelets of gold﴾ "asawir" is the plural of "siwar" (bracelet), ﴿and pearls﴾. The people of Madinah and 'Asim read "wa-lu'lu'an" here and in Surah al-Mala'ikah (Surah 35) in the accusative, agreeing with Ya'qub here, on the meaning "and they will be adorned with pearls," and because it is written with an alif in the codices. The others read it in the genitive, coordinating it with his words "min dhahab" (of gold). Abu Ja'far and Abu Bakr omit the first hamza throughout the Qur'an. They differed over the reason for the alif written in it: Abu 'Amr said: they wrote it as they wrote it in "qalu" and "kanu" (where the alif is retained). Al-Kisa'i said: they wrote it for the hamza, because the hamza is a letter among the letters. ﴿And their clothing therein is silk﴾ That is: they will wear in Paradise garments of silk brocade, which is the very thing forbidden to men to wear in this world.

Abd al-Wahid al-Malihi informed us, Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Shurayh informed us, Abu al-Qasim al-Baghawi informed us, Ali ibn al-Ja'd informed us, Shu'bah informed us, from Qatadah, from Dawud al-Sarraj, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, from the Prophet (ﷺ) who said: "Whoever wears silk in this world will not be given it to wear in the Hereafter; and if he enters Paradise, the people of Paradise will wear it, but he will not wear it." [[Narrated by al-Hakim: 4/191, who authenticated it and al-Dhahabi agreed; and Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi, p. 294, and he also narrated it from Umar (may Allah be pleased with him), p. 10. The two Shaykhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim) narrated it from Anas ibn Malik with the wording: "Whoever wears silk in this world will not wear it in the Hereafter": al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Libas, Bab Libas al-Harir lil-Rijal: 10/284; and Muslim, Kitab al-Libas, Bab Tahrim al-Dhahab wa'l-Harir ala'l-Rijal wa-Ibahatihi lil-Nisa', no. (2073), 3/1645; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 12/30–31.]]

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 22, verses 24–25:

His saying, mighty and majestic is He: ﴿And they were guided to the good word﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: it is the testimony that there is no god but Allah. Ibn Zayd said: "There is no god but Allah, Allah is greatest, and praise belongs to Allah [and glory be to Allah]" [an addition from manuscript "b"]. As-Suddi said: that is, the Qur'an. It was also said: it is the saying of the people of Paradise: "Praise belongs to Allah, who has fulfilled His promise to us" (az-Zumar 39:74). ﴿And they were guided to the path of the Praiseworthy﴾: to the religion of Allah, which is Islam. "The Praiseworthy" is Allah, who is praised in His actions.

His saying, mighty and majestic is He: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve and bar [others] from the way of Allah﴾. He placed the present tense (al-mustaqbal) after the past tense (al-madi), because the meaning of the present-tense form is the past, as He said in another place: ﴿Those who disbelieve and bar [others] from the way of Allah﴾ (an-Nisa' 4:167). The meaning is: those who disbelieved previously, and who now bar [others] from the way of Allah, that is, while they are barring.

﴿And the Sacred Mosque﴾: that is, and they bar [others] from the Sacred Mosque.

﴿which We have made for the people﴾: a qiblah for their prayer, and a place of rites (mansak) and of worship (mut'abbad), as He said: ﴿It was placed for the people﴾ (Al 'Imran 3:96).

﴿Equal﴾: Hafs, on the authority of 'Asim, and Ya'qub read "sawa'an" in the accusative, with the action of "making" falling upon it, because the verb ja'ala (to make) takes two objects. It was also said: its meaning is "equal in it," so that ﴿the one who dwells there and the visitor﴾ [are equal]. The rest of the readers read it in the nominative, as the subject (mubtada'), with what follows it as the predicate (khabar), and the complete sentence ends at His saying "for the people." By "al-'akif" (the one who dwells there) he meant the one who resides in it, and by "al-badi" (the visitor) he meant the one who arrives at it and comes to it from elsewhere.

The scholars differed concerning the meaning of the verse. A group said: "equal are the one who dwells there and the visitor" means equal in honouring its sanctity and in performing the rites within it. This was the view of Mujahid, al-Hasan and a group, and they said: what is meant is the Sacred Mosque itself. The meaning of the equality is equality in honouring the Ka'bah, in the merit of prayer in the Sacred Mosque, and in circumambulation of the House.

Others said: what is meant is the whole Sacred Precinct (al-Haram), and the meaning of the equality is that the resident and the visitor are equal in lodging there; neither of them has a greater right to a dwelling than the other, except that no one is to be driven out of a dwelling once he has taken possession of it. This is the view of Ibn 'Abbas, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Qatadah and Ibn Zayd. They said: the two are equal in [the houses] [in "b": the markets] and dwellings.

'Abd al-Rahman ibn Sabit said: when the pilgrims came to Makkah, none of the people of Makkah had a greater right to his dwelling than they did. 'Umar ibn al-Khattab used to forbid people from closing their doors during the season (al-mawsim). According to this view, the sale and rental of houses in Makkah is not permissible. According to the first view, which is closer to the truth, it is permissible, because Allah the Exalted said: ﴿those who were expelled from their homes﴾ (al-Hajj 22:40). The Prophet (ﷺ) said on the day of the Conquest of Makkah: "Whoever enters the house of Abu Sufyan is safe" [a portion of a hadith narrated by Muslim in the Book of Jihad and Expeditions, chapter: The Conquest of Makkah, no. 1780, 3/1405–1407]. Thus he attributed the house to him by way of ownership. 'Umar also bought a house in Makkah to serve as a prison for four thousand dirhams, which indicates the permissibility of selling it. This is the view of Tawus and 'Amr ibn Dinar, and al-Shafi'i also held it.

His saying, mighty and majestic is He: ﴿And whoever intends therein deviation through wrongdoing﴾: that is, within the Sacred Mosque, deviation through wrongdoing, which is inclination toward injustice. The "ba'" in His saying "bi-ilhad" (through deviation) is superfluous (za'idah), like His saying: ﴿grows with the oil﴾ (al-Mu'minun 23:20). Its meaning is: whoever intends therein deviation through wrongdoing. al-A'sha said: "Our spears guaranteed the provision of our dependants," meaning the provision of our dependants. al-Mubarrad denied that the "ba'" is superfluous and said: the meaning of the verse is "whoever's intention therein is to deviate through wrongdoing."

They differed concerning this deviation. Mujahid and Qatadah said: it is shirk and the worship of other than Allah.

A group said: it is everything that was forbidden, whether of speech or action, even insulting a servant.

'Ata' said: it is entering the Sacred Precinct without being in a state of ihram, or committing any of the prohibited acts of the Haram, such as killing game or cutting trees.

Ibn 'Abbas said: it is that you kill in it one who does not kill you, or wrong in it one who does not wrong you. This is also the meaning of the saying of ad-Dahhak.

It is related from Mujahid that he said: sins are multiplied in Makkah just as good deeds are multiplied.

Habib ibn Abi Thabit said: it is hoarding food in Makkah.

'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, regarding His saying: ﴿And whoever intends therein deviation through wrongdoing, We shall make him taste a painful punishment﴾, said: if a man were to resolve upon a sin, it would not be recorded against him so long as he did not commit it; but if a man were to resolve to kill a man in Makkah while he was in 'Adan Abyan, or in another land, Allah would make him taste a painful punishment. As-Suddi said: except that he repents.

It is related from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar that he had two tents, one in the non-sacred territory (al-Hill) and the other in the Haram. When he wished to rebuke his family, he would rebuke them in the other one. When he was asked about this, he said: "We used to be told that among deviation within it is that a man says: 'No, by Allah,' and 'Yes, by Allah'" [al-Tabari mentioned these views: 17/138–142, then said: the most correct of the views we have mentioned concerning the interpretation of this is the view related from Ibn Mas'ud and Ibn 'Abbas, that "wrongdoing" here refers to every act of disobedience to Allah, because Allah spoke generally with His saying "whoever intends therein deviation through wrongdoing," and did not restrict wrongdoing to one kind over another, whether in good or in reason, so it remains general].

The commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 22, verses 26–27:

His, the Mighty and Majestic, saying: ﴿And [mention] when We settled for Abraham the place of the House﴾, meaning: We made it ready. Ibn Abbas said: We made it. It is also said: We showed it. Al-Zajjaj said: We made the place of the House a settling place (mubawwa'an) for Abraham.

Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: We prepared it. We mentioned "the place of the House" [[The text between the brackets is absent from manuscript "A".]] because the Ka'bah was raised up to the heavens at the time of the Flood. Then, when God the Exalted commanded Abraham to build the House, he did not know where to build it, so God sent a strong wind that swept clear the area around the House down to its foundation. [[See al-Tabari: 17/143.]]

Al-Kalbi said: God sent a cloud the size of the House, and it stood above the site of the House, and in it there was a head that spoke: "O Abraham, build upon my measure." So he built upon it. [[See al-Durr al-Manthur: 6/30.]]

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿That you shall not associate anything with Me﴾, meaning: We entrusted Abraham and said to him, "Do not associate anything with Me." ﴿And purify My House for those who circumambulate﴾, meaning those who circle around the House; ﴿and those who stand [in prayer]﴾, meaning those who remain [there]; ﴿and those who bow and prostrate﴾, meaning those who pray.

﴿And proclaim to the people the pilgrimage﴾, meaning: inform them and call out to the people, ﴿for the Hajj﴾. Abraham said, "And how will my voice reach [them]?" He said, "Upon you is the proclamation, and upon Me is the delivery." So Abraham stood on the Maqam, and the Maqam rose until it became like the tallest of mountains. He placed his two fingers in his ears and turned his face right and left, east and west, and said: "O people, indeed your Lord has built a House and has prescribed upon you the Hajj to the House, so answer your Lord." So everyone who was destined to make the pilgrimage, from the loins of fathers and the wombs of mothers, responded: "Here I am, O God, here I am." [[See al-Tabari: 17/144.]] Ibn Abbas said: The first to respond to him were the people of Yemen, for they are the most numerous of the people in pilgrimage.

It is also narrated that Abraham ascended Abu Qubays and called out. [[Cited by al-Suyuti: 6/35 to Ibn Abi Hatim from Ibn Abbas.]] Ibn Abbas said: By "the people" in this verse is meant the people of the qiblah. Al-Hasan claimed that His saying, "And proclaim to the people the pilgrimage," is a separate new statement, and that the one commanded to make this proclamation was Muhammad (ﷺ), who was commanded to do so during the Farewell Pilgrimage.

Abu Hurayrah narrated that he said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "O people, the Hajj has been made obligatory upon you, so perform the Hajj." [[Narrated by Muslim in the Book of Hajj, chapter: The obligation of Hajj once in a lifetime, no. 1337, 2/975, and by the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 7/3.]]

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿They will come to you on foot﴾, meaning walking on their feet. Rijal is the plural of rajil, like qa'im and qiyam, and sa'im and siyam. ﴿And on every lean camel﴾, meaning riding upon every lean camel. Al-dami is the emaciated camel.

﴿They will come from every deep mountain pass﴾, meaning from every distant path. The reason that "ya'tina" is in the feminine plural is because of the word "kull" (every) and the intention of the she-camels (nuq).

**﴿and mention the name of Allah on known days﴾** means the first ten days of Dhu al-Hijjah, according to the view of most exegetes. They were called "known" (ma'lumat) because of the eagerness to know their count, owing to the time of the Hajj at their end. It is narrated from Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, that they are the day of sacrifice (yawm al-nahr) and the three days after it. Allah said this because the people of the pre-Islamic period (jahiliyyah) would not eat anything from the meat of their offerings. Abu Abd Allah Muhammad ibn al-Fadl al-Khirqi informed us; Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Abd Allah al-Taysafuni informed us; Abd Allah ibn Umar al-Jawhari informed us; Ahmad ibn Ali al-Kushmihani informed us; Ali ibn Hujr informed us; Isma'il ibn Ja'far informed us; from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Jabir ibn Abd Allah, who said, in the account of the Farewell Pilgrimage: "Ali came with camels from Yemen, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) drove a hundred camels. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) slaughtered sixty-three of them with his own hand, and Ali slaughtered the rest. Then the Prophet (ﷺ) ordered that a piece from every camel be taken and placed in a pot, and they both ate from its meat and drank from its broth."[[A portion of the hadith of Jabir, related by Muslim, no. 1218: 2/893, and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 7/150.]]

The scholars differed concerning the hady that is obligatory by the Law: is it permissible for the one offering it to eat any of it? Such as the hady of tamattu' (combining Umrah and Hajj), the hady of qiran (combining both in one ihram), the obligatory hady for spoiling the Hajj or for missing it (fawat), and the compensation for hunting game (jaza' al-sayd)?

One group held that it is not permissible for him to eat any of it, and this is the view of al-Shafi'i. The same applies to what he made obligatory upon himself by vow (nadhr). Ibn Umar said: he does not eat from the compensation for hunting or from the vowed offering, but he eats from what is other than that. This is also the view of Ahmad and Ishaq. Malik said: he eats from the hady of tamattu' and from every hady that became obligatory upon him, except the expiation for harm (fidyat al-adha), the compensation for hunting, and the vowed offering. According to the adherents of opinion (ashab al-ra'y), he eats from the hady of tamattu' and qiran, and does not eat from any other obligatory hady apart from these two.

The Exalted and Majestic said: **﴿and feed the miserable, the poor﴾**, meaning the disabled poor person who has nothing. The "miserable" (ba'is) is one whose destitution has become severe, and bu's (destitution) is severe poverty.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 22, verse 29:

﴿Then let them complete their rites (tafath)﴾ Tafath means filth and dirt arising from long hair, long nails and unkempt appearance. The Arabs say to someone whom they find disgusting: "Mā atfathaka!", meaning: "How dirty you are!" The pilgrim (hajj) is dishevelled and dust-covered, having not shaved his hair nor trimmed his nails, so qada' al-tafath (fulfilling the tafath) means removing these things, "that they may remove their dirt." What is intended is exiting the state of ihram (the sacred state of pilgrimage) by shaving, trimming the moustache, plucking the armpit hair, using a depilatory, cutting the nails and changing into ordinary clothes. Ibn 'Umar and Ibn 'Abbas said: "Qada' al-tafath" means all the rites of the Hajj. Mujahid said: it means the rites of the Hajj, taking from the moustache, plucking the armpit hair, shaving the pubic area and cutting the nails. It was also said: tafath here means the stoning of the jamarat (pillars). Al-Zajjaj said: "We do not know tafath and its meaning except from the Qur'an."

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And let them fulfil their vows﴾ Mujahid said: it refers to the vow of Hajj and the sacrifice, and whatever a person vows of anything that pertains to the Hajj; that is, that they complete these by fulfilling them. It was also said: what is intended is fulfilling what one has vowed, in its apparent sense. It was also said: what is intended is discharging what is obligatory upon one, whether one has vowed or not. The Arabs say of anyone who discharges what is obligatory upon him that he "fulfilled his vow." 'Asim, in the narration of Abu Bakr, read "wa-liyuwaffū" with a fatha on the waw and a shadda on the fa'.

﴿And let them circumambulate the Ancient House﴾ It refers to the obligatory circumambulation, which is the circumambulation of ifada (departure) on the Day of Sacrifice after the stoning and shaving.

Circumambulation is of three kinds. The first is the circumambulation of arrival (tawaf al-qudum): whoever arrives in Makkah circles the House seven times, performing ramal (a brisk trot) for three rounds from the Black Stone until he returns to it, and walking for four. This circumambulation is a sunnah (recommended practice), and there is nothing upon one who omits it.

Abu 'Isa Ahmad informed us... (chain as follows) Ibn Wahb informed us, 'Amr ibn al-Harith informed us, from Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Nawfal al-Qurashi, that he asked 'Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, saying: "The Prophet (ﷺ) performed Hajj." Then 'Ā'ishah informed me that the first thing he began with when he arrived was that he performed wudu, then circumambulated the House, and then there was no 'umrah. Then Abu Bakr performed Hajj, and the first thing he began with was circumambulating the House, and then there was no 'umrah. Then 'Umar did the same. Then 'Uthman performed Hajj, and I saw that the first thing he began with was circumambulating the House. [Reported by al-Bukhari in al-Hajj, chapter: Circumambulation in a state of wudu: 3/496; and Muslim in al-Hajj, chapter: What is required of one who circumambulates the House and performs sa'y, no. 1235, 2/906-907; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 7/101-102.]

Al-Kisa'i informed us, 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Ahmad al-Khallal informed us, Abu al-'Abbas al-Asamm informed us, al-Rabi' informed us, al-Shafi'i informed us, Anas ibn 'Iyad informed us, from Musa ibn 'Uqbah, from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), that when he circumambulated during Hajj or 'umrah upon first arriving, he would hasten (ramal) for three circuits and walk for four, then he would pray two rak'ahs, then he would go between al-Safa and al-Marwah seven times. [Reported by al-Bukhari in al-Hajj, chapter: Whoever circumambulates the House upon arriving in Makkah: 3/477; Muslim in al-Hajj, chapter: Recommendation of ramal in tawaf and 'umrah, no. 1261, 2/920; the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 7/104; and al-Shafi'i in al-Musnad: 1/347.]

The second circumambulation is the circumambulation of ifada on the Day of Sacrifice after the stoning and shaving. It is obligatory, and one does not exit the state of ihram until one has performed it.

Abdul-Wahid al-Maliḥi informed us, Ahmad al-Nu'aymi informed us, Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us, 'Umar ibn Hafs informed us, my father informed us, al-A'mash informed us, Ibrahim informed us, from al-Aswad, from 'Ā'ishah, who said: "Safiyyah menstruated on the night of departure, and she said: 'I think I am only detaining you.' The Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'Aqra, halqa! Did she circumambulate on the Day of Sacrifice?' It was said: 'Yes.' He said: 'Then depart.'" [Reported by al-Bukhari in al-Hajj, chapter: Hastening from al-Muhassab: 3/595; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 7/234.] From this it is established that whoever does not perform the circumambulation of ifada on the Day of Sacrifice is not permitted to depart.

The third circumambulation is the circumambulation of farewell (tawaf al-wada'). There is no concession in it for one who wishes to leave Makkah for a distance of qasr (shortening of prayer): he may not leave until he has circumambulated the House seven times. Whoever omits it must offer a sacrifice (dam), except a menstruating woman, who is permitted to omit the circumambulation of farewell.

Abdul-Wahhab ibn Muhammad al-Khatib informed us, 'Abd al-'Aziz Ahmad al-Khallal informed us, Abu al-'Abbas al-Asamm informed us, al-Rabi' informed us, al-Shafi'i informed us, Sufyan informed us, from Sulayman al-Ahwal, from Tawus, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "The people were commanded that the last of their obligations should be circumambulating the House, except that a menstruating woman was granted a concession." [Reported by al-Bukhari in al-Hajj, chapter: Tawaf al-wada': 3/585; Muslim in al-Hajj, chapter: The obligation of tawaf al-wada' and its waiver for the menstruating woman, no. 1328; the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 7/232; and al-Shafi'i in al-Musnad: 1/364.]

Ramal is specific to the circumambulation of arrival; there is no ramal in the circumambulation of ifada or of farewell.

His saying: ﴿the Ancient House﴾ The scholars differed regarding the meaning of "al-'Atiq." Ibn 'Abbas, Ibn al-Zubayr, Mujahid and Qatadah said: it was called "ancient" because Allah freed it (a'taqahu) from the hands of tyrants, so that they could not reach its destruction; no tyrant ever prevailed over it. Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah said: it was called "ancient" because it was never owned. Al-Hasan and Ibn Zayd said: it was named thus because it is ancient, being the first House set down for mankind; one says "dinar 'atiq," meaning an old dinar. It was also said: it was named "ancient" because Allah freed it from drowning, for it was raised up during the days of the Flood. [These statements are mentioned by al-Tabari: 17/151-152, and he then said: "Each of these statements attributed to those whom we have mentioned regarding His saying 'the Ancient House' has a valid aspect, though what Ibn Zayd said is most apparent in its outward meaning; yet what is related from Ibn al-Zubayr is more authentic, if what Muhammad ibn Sahl al-Bukhari related to me is correct: he said: 'Abdullah ibn Salih told us, he said: al-Layth informed me, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Khalid ibn Musafir, from al-Zuhri, from Muhammad ibn 'Urwah, from 'Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr, who said: the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The House was only named 'the Ancient' because Allah freed it from the tyrants, so that it was never overcome, sound.""]

**That is so. Whoever honours the sacred rites of God, it is better for him with his Lord.** That is, the matter is so, meaning what was mentioned of the rites of the Hajj. **And whoever honours the sacred prohibitions of God** means the disobediences of God and what He has forbidden. Honouring them is abstaining from engaging in them. Al-Layth said: The sacred prohibitions of God are those things whose violation is not permitted. Al-Zajjaj said: *al-hurmah* (sanctity) is that which must be upheld and whose neglect is forbidden. Some people held that the meaning of *al-hurumat* (sacred prohibitions) here is the rites (*al-manasik*), based on the verses that are connected to it. Ibn Zayd said: The sacred prohibitions here are the Sacred House, the sacred land, the sacred month, the Sacred Mosque, and the state of *ihram* [[See al-Tabari: 17/153.]].

**It is better for him with his Lord** means: honouring the sacred prohibitions is better for him with God in the Hereafter.

His saying, Exalted and Majestic is He: **And the grazing livestock has been made lawful for you**, to eat them when you slaughter them, and they are camels, cattle and sheep. **Except what is recited to you** as prohibited, which is His saying in Surat al-Ma'idah: **Prohibited to you are carrion, blood** [Q. 5:3], to the end of the verse. **So avoid the filth of idols**, meaning their worship. It says: Keep away from them, for they are filth, that is, a cause of filth, which is punishment. *Al-rijs* has the same meaning as *al-rijz*. Al-Zajjaj said: *min* (مِنْ) here is *li-l-tajnis* (denoting the genus), meaning: avoid the idols, which are filth. **And avoid the word of falsehood**, meaning lying and slander. Ibn Mas'ud said: It is false testimony. It is narrated that the Prophet (ﷺ) stood up to give a sermon and said: "O people, false testimony has been equated with associating partners with God," then he recited this verse [[Narrated by Abu Dawud in al-Aqdiyah, chapter on false testimony: 5/217; al-Tirmidhi in al-Shahadat 6/585, and he said: "This is a hadith which we only know from the hadith of Sufyan ibn Ziyad, meaning the hadith of Khuraym ibn Fatik, and they differed in the narration of this hadith from Sufyan ibn Ziyad, and we do not know that Ayman ibn Khuraym heard from the Prophet (ﷺ)." And Ibn Majah in al-Ahkam, chapter: false testimony, no. (2372), 2/794; and Imam Ahmad: 4/178.]]. It was also said: It is the saying of the polytheists in their talbiyah: "Here I am, O God, here I am; You have no partner, except a partner who belongs to You, You own him and what he owns."

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 22, verse 31:

﴿Ḥunafā’ lillāh﴾ — sincere devotees to Him (mukhliṣīn lahu), ﴿not associating anything with Him﴾. Qatadah said: "They used to make the pilgrimage (ḥajj) while in polytheism, and they would forbid (themselves) daughters, mothers and sisters, and they were called ḥunafā’. Then this was revealed: 'Ḥunafā’ for Allah, not associating anything with Him,' meaning: pilgrims for Allah, submitting and affirming His oneness (muwaḥḥidīn). That is, whoever associates partners with Allah cannot be a ḥanīf."

﴿And whoever associates partners with Allah, it is as if he had fallen﴾ — that is, he dropped, ﴿from the sky﴾ — to the earth, ﴿and the birds snatch him away﴾ — that is, the birds seize him and carry him off. The words khaṭf and ikhtiṭāf mean taking hold of a thing swiftly. The people of Madinah recited it as fa-takhaṭṭafuhu, with a fatha on the kha’ and a shadda on the ṭā’, meaning yatakhaṭṭafuhu. ﴿Or the wind carries him off﴾ — that is, it sways him and takes him away, ﴿to a distant place﴾.

That is, far away. Its meaning: the distance of the one who associates partners from the truth is like the distance of one who has fallen from the sky, whom the birds have snatched or the wind has hurled down, so that he can never reach it in any way. It has also been said: the state of the polytheist is likened to the state of one falling from the sky, in that he has no means to save himself until the wind casts him where it will; he is thus certainly destroyed, either by the birds tearing at his flesh or by his falling into the distant place. Al-Hasan said: the deeds of the disbelievers are likened to this state, in that they go away and become void, so they have power over nothing of them.

﴿That﴾ means: what I mentioned of avoiding filth (*rijs*) and false speech. ﴿And whoever honours the rites (*sha'a'ir*) of God, then indeed it is from the piety of the hearts﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: "The rites of God" are the camels and the sacrificial animals (*hady*). Their origin is from *al-ish'ar*, which is marking them so that it is known that they are sacrificial animals. Honouring them means fattening them and choosing good ones for them. It was also said: "The rites of God" are the signs of His religion. "Then indeed it is from the piety of the hearts," meaning: indeed, honouring them is from the piety of the hearts.

﴿For you in them﴾ means: in the camels, before they are designated as sacrificial animals, ﴿there are benefits﴾ in their milk, their offspring, their wool, their hair, and riding on their backs, ﴿until a specified term﴾. That term is when one designates them and makes them obligatory as sacrificial animals. If he does that, he has no right to any of their benefits. This is the statement of Mujahid, and the statement of Qatadah and al-Dahhak, and Muqsim narrated it from Ibn 'Abbas.

It was also said: its meaning is that for you, in the sacrificial animals, there are benefits after making them obligatory and designating them as sacrificial animals, by riding them and drinking their milk when there is need, ﴿until a specified term﴾, meaning: until you slaughter them. This is the statement of 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah.

The scholars differed concerning riding the sacrificial animal.

Some people said: it is permissible for him to ride them and to load them, so long as this does not harm them. This is the view of Malik, al-Shafi'i, Ahmad, and Ishaq, based on what Abu al-Hasan al-Sarakhsi informed us: Abu 'Ali Zahir ibn Ahmad informed us: Abu Ishaq al-Hashimi informed us: Abu Mus'ab informed us, from Malik, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) saw a man driving a camel, and he said to him: "Ride it." The man said: "O Messenger of God, it is a camel (designated for sacrifice)." He said: "Ride it, woe to you," at the second or third time. And likewise he said to him: "Drink its milk after what is left over from the satisfaction of its young." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Hajj, chapter: Riding the camels (*budn*), 3/536; and Muslim in al-Hajj, chapter: The permissibility of riding the camel offered as a sacrifice for one who is in need of it, no. (1322), 2/960; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 7/195.]]

The people of opinion (*ashab al-ra'y*) said: he should not ride it.

Some people said: he should not ride it except when he is compelled to do so.

Some of them said: by the rites he meant the rituals (*manasik*) and beholding Makkah. ﴿For you in them there are benefits﴾ through trade and markets, ﴿until a specified term﴾, which is leaving Makkah.

It was also said: ﴿For you in them there are benefits﴾ in reward and recompense for performing the rituals, ﴿until a specified term﴾, meaning: until the end of the days of the Hajj.

﴿Then their place of sacrifice﴾, meaning: their place of slaughter, ﴿is at the Ancient House﴾, meaning: their slaughter is at the Ancient House, intending the entire land of the Sacred Precinct (*haram*), just as He said: ﴿So let them not approach the Sacred Mosque﴾ (al-Tawbah: 28), meaning: the entire Sacred Precinct.

It is narrated from Jabir, in the account of the Farewell Pilgrimage, that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "I slaughtered here, and all of Mina is a place of slaughter, so slaughter in your encampments." [[Narrated by Muslim in al-Hajj, chapter: That all of 'Arafah is a place of standing, no. (1218), 2/893; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 7/150.]]

Whoever said that "the rites" are the rituals said: the meaning of His words "Then their place of sacrifice is at the Ancient House" is: the place where people become free from their state of ihram is at the Ancient House, meaning: that they circumambulate it with the circumambulation of increase (*tawaf al-ziyarah*) on the Day of Sacrifice. [27a]

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And for every community﴾, that is, every community of believers that came before you, ﴿We have appointed a rite (mansak)﴾. Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read the sin here and at the end of the surah with a kasra (مَنْسِكًا, misik), taking it as a noun of place like "al-masjid" and "al-matla'," meaning a place of sacrifice (madhbah), which is the site of the offering. The others read it with a fatha on the sin, as a verbal noun (masdar), like "al-mudkhal" and "al-mukhraj," meaning the shedding of blood and the slaughter of offerings. ﴿That they may mention the name of Allah over what He has provided for them of the beast of cattle﴾ [at the time of its slaughtering and sacrificing]. He called it "beast" (bahimah) because it does not speak. He said "beast of cattle" and restricted it to livestock (al-an'am), because among beasts there are those that are not of the cattle, such as horses, mules and donkeys, and it is not permissible to offer them as sacrifices.

﴿So your God is one God﴾, that is: mention the name of Allah alone over the slaughtered animals, for your God is one God. ﴿So to Him submit﴾, that is, yield and obey. ﴿And give good tidings to the humble (al-mukhbitin)﴾. Ibn 'Abbas and Qatadah said: the humble. Mujahid said: those who are at peace (mutma'innin) with Allah, Mighty and Majestic; "al-khabt" is the lowland, the depressed part of the earth. Al-Akhfash said: the submissive. Al-Nakha'i said: the sincere. Al-Kalbi said: they are those whose hearts are tender. 'Amr ibn Aws said: they are those who do not wrong, and when they are wronged, do not seek vengeance.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 22, verse 35–36:

﴿Those who, when Allah is mentioned, their hearts tremble, and those who endure patiently what befalls them﴾ of trials and calamities, ﴿and those who establish the prayer﴾, i.e., those who establish the prayer at its appointed times, ﴿and from what We have provided them they spend﴾, i.e., they give charity.

His saying, mighty and majestic is He: ﴿al-budn﴾ is the plural of badanah (camel sacrificed as an offering), so called for its largeness and bulk. It refers to large camels, sound in body. It is said: badina al-rajul budnan and badanah (the man became heavy/stout) when he grew large; but when he grew old and flaccid, it is said badana tabdinan. ʿAtaʾ and al-Suddi said: al-budn are camels and cows; sheep are not called badanah.

﴿We have made them for you among the symbols of Allah﴾, i.e., among the markers of His religion. They are called shaʿaʾir (symbols, sing. shaʿirah) because they are marked (tushʿar), which is that the animal is stabbed with an iron tool in its hump so that it is known to be an offering (hady). ﴿For you therein is good﴾: benefit in this world and reward in the Hereafter. ﴿So mention the name of Allah over them﴾ at their slaughter. ﴿Standing in lines (ṣawāff)﴾, i.e., standing on three legs, with their two hind legs and one foreleg bound together, while the left foreleg is tied, and so it is slaughtered in that manner.

ʿAbd al-Wahid al-Maliḥi related to us, Ahmad ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Nuʿaymi related to us, Muhammad ibn Yusuf related to us, Muhammad ibn Isma'il related to us, ʿAbd Allah ibn Maslamah related to us, Yazid ibn Zurayʿ related to us, from Yunus, from Ziyad ibn Jubayr who said: I saw Ibn ʿUmar come upon a man who had made his camel kneel to slaughter it. He said: "Send it forth standing, tied, the Sunnah of Muhammad ﷺ." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Hajj, chapter: Slaughtering camels tied; 3/553; and Muslim in al-Hajj, chapter: Slaughtering the budn standing and tied, no. (1320) 2/956; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 7/198.]]

Mujahid said: al-Ṣawwaf is when its left leg is tied and it stands on three legs.

Ibn Masʿud read: "ṣawāfin," meaning that one of its forelegs is tied and it is slaughtered on three, and it is like ṣawāff. Ubayy, al-Hasan and Mujahid read: "ṣawāfī" with a yā', meaning: purified and sincere, belonging to Allah, with no partner in it.

﴿So when their flanks fall (wajabat junubuha)﴾, i.e., they fall after slaughter, so their sides come down upon the ground. The root of wujub is falling: it is said wajabat al-shams when the sun sets (falls for setting). ﴿So eat from them﴾: a command of permission. ﴿And feed the one who is content and the one who is in need (al-qani' wal-mu'tarr)﴾. They differed over their meanings:

ʿIkrimah, Ibrahim and Qatadah said: "al-qani'" is the one who sits in his house, abstaining (mutaʿaffif), who is content with what is given and does not ask, and "al-muʿtarr" is the one who asks.

Al-ʿAwfi related from Ibn ʿAbbas: "al-qani'" is the one who does not approach or ask, and "al-muʿtarr" is the one who shows himself and presents himself without asking. According to these two interpretations, "al-qani'" is from qana'ah (contentment): it is said qani'a qana'atan when he was pleased with what was apportioned to him.

﴿We have made them for you among the symbols of Allah﴾, i.e., among the markers of His religion. Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 22, verse 37:

﴿It is not their flesh, nor their blood, that reaches Allah﴾. This is because the people of the Jahiliyyah (the pre-Islamic period of ignorance) used to slaughter the budn (camels offered as sacrificial animals) and smear the Ka'bah with their blood, seeking nearness to Allah. So Allah revealed this verse: "It is not their flesh, nor their blood, that reaches Allah."

Ya'qub read "تَنَالُ وَتَنَالُهُ" with the letter ta' in both places, while the majority of readers read them with the letter ya'.

Muqatil said: "Their flesh and their blood will not be raised up to Allah. ﴿But it is piety from you that reaches Him﴾. Rather, the righteous deeds, piety, and sincerity from you, which are intended for the Face of Allah, are raised up to Him."

﴿Thus He has subjected them to you﴾, meaning the budn, ﴿so that you may glorify Allah for having guided you﴾, that is, guided you to the landmarks of His religion and the rites of His Hajj. This is by saying: "Allah is the Greatest, for having guided us, and all praise is due to Allah for having tested us and bestowed upon us."

﴿And give good news to the muhsinun (those who do good)﴾. Ibn Abbas said: they are the muwahhidun (those who affirm the oneness of Allah).

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 22, verses 38–39:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, Allah defends those who have believed﴾. Ibn Kathir and the people of Basra read "yadfa'u" (yadfa'u), while the others read "yudafi'u" (yudafi'u) with an alif, meaning: He repels the evil (ghā'ila) of the polytheists from the believers and keeps them away from the believers.

﴿Indeed, Allah does not love every treacherous ingrate﴾. That is: treacherous regarding the trust of Allah, ungrateful for His blessing. Ibn Abbas said: They betrayed Allah by setting up a partner with Him, and they denied His blessings. Al-Zajjaj said: Whoever draws near to idols with his sacrifice and mentions over it the name of other than Allah, he is a treacherous ingrate.

His saying, mighty and majestic is He: ﴿Permission has been given to those who are being fought, because they were wronged﴾. The people of Medina, Basra and 'Asim read "udhina" (udhina) with a damma on the alif, and the rest read it with a fatha, meaning: Allah has given permission. "Li-lladhina yuqatilun": the people of Medina, Ibn Amir and Hafs read "yuqatalun" (yuqatalun) with a fatha on the ta', meaning the believers who are being fought by the polytheists; and the others read it with a kasra on the ta', meaning those to whom permission for jihad was given, who "yuqatilun" (yuqatilun) the polytheists.

The exegetes said: The polytheists of Mecca used to harm the companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), so they would continually be grieved by those who were beaten and wounded, and they would complain of that to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). He would say to them: "Be patient, for I have not been commanded to fight," until the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) emigrated, and then Allah, mighty and majestic, revealed this verse. [[Ibn Hajar said in al-Kafi al-Shaf, p. (113): I have not found it in this form. Al-Wahidi attributed it in al-Wasit to the exegetes. I say - Ibn Hajar: It is drawn from hadiths, the closest of which is what Ibn Abi Hatim narrated through the route of Bukayr ibn Ma'ruf from Muqatil ibn Hayyan, his saying: (Permission has been given to those who are being fought, because they were wronged). That is because the polytheists of Mecca used to harm the Muslims in Mecca, so they sought the permission of the Prophet (ﷺ) to fight them in Mecca, but the Prophet (ﷺ) forbade them from that. Mujahid said: This verse was revealed concerning specific people who went out as emigrants from Mecca to Medina, and they were being prevented, so Allah gave them permission to fight the disbelievers who were preventing them from emigrating. Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 22, verse 40–41:

﴿Those who have been expelled from their homes without right — only because they say, "Our Lord is Allah."﴾ It is a substitute (badal) for the first "those who" (alladhina). That is: they were not expelled from their homes except because of their saying, "Our Lord is Allah" alone.

﴿And had it not been for Allah's repelling of people, some by means of others﴾ — by means of jihad and the establishment of the prescribed punishments (hudud) — ﴿then would have been demolished﴾. The people of the Hijaz read it with a light (takhfif) dal, while the others read it with a doubled (tashdid) dal, indicating intensification (ta'thir). The light form is used for a small quantity and for abundance, whereas the doubled form is specific to abundance. ﴿Monasteries (sawami')﴾: Mujahid and al-Dahhak said: it means the monasteries of the monks. Qatadah said: the monasteries of the Sabians. ﴿And churches (bi'a')﴾: the churches of the Christians, the plural of "bay'ah," which is the church of the Christians. ﴿And synagogues (salawat)﴾: meaning the synagogues of the Jews, which they call in Hebrew "salwta." ﴿And mosques in which the name of Allah is much mentioned﴾: meaning the mosques of the Muslims of the community of Muhammad (ﷺ).

The meaning of the verse: And had it not been for Allah's repelling of people, some by means of others, the place of their prayer would have been demolished in the law of every prophet — in the time of Musa the synagogues would have been demolished, in the time of Isa the churches and monasteries, and in the time of Muhammad (ﷺ) the mosques.

Ibn Zayd said: by "salawat" he meant the prayers of the people of Islam, for they are interrupted when the enemy enters upon them.

﴿And Allah will surely support those who support Him﴾: that is, who support His religion and His Prophet. ﴿Indeed, Allah is Strong and Mighty.﴾ ﴿Those who, if We establish them in the land, establish prayer, give zakat, enjoin what is right, and forbid what is wrong.﴾ Al-Zajjaj said: this is a description of His supporters. The meaning of "We establish them in the land" is: We grant them victory over their enemy until they become firmly settled in the lands. Qatadah said: they are the companions of Muhammad (ﷺ). Al-Hasan said: they are this community. ﴿And to Allah belongs the outcome of all matters﴾: that is, the final end of the affairs of creation and their return is to Him; meaning, every kingdom other than His kingdom will be nullified, so affairs will return to Him without any contender or claimant.

﴿How many a town did We destroy﴾, "how many" meaning "how much." ﴿while it was wrongdoing﴾, meaning its people were wrongdoers, ﴿so it lies fallen on its trellises﴾, meaning fallen upon its roofs, ﴿and [how many] an abandoned well﴾ [meaning: how many an abandoned well], left, neglected and empty of its people, ﴿and a lofty palace﴾. **Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 22, verses 46–47:**

﴿Have they not traveled through the earth?﴾ Meaning: the disbelievers of Makkah, so that they might look upon the places of ruin of the deniers from the earlier nations. ﴿So that they would have hearts with which they understand, or ears with which they hear.﴾ Meaning: what is related to them of the reports of the past generations, so that they might take warning from them. ﴿Indeed, it is not the eyes that go blind, but it is the hearts within the breasts that go blind.﴾ He mentioned "within the breasts" for emphasis, like His saying: ﴿flying with its two wings﴾ (Al-An'am: 38). The meaning is that the harmful blindness is blindness of the heart. As for blindness of the eyes, it is not harmful in matters of religion. Qatadah said: "The outward sight is merely provision and enjoyment, while the sight of the heart is the beneficial sight."

﴿And they ask you to hasten the punishment.﴾ It was revealed concerning al-Nadr ibn al-Harith, when he said: "If this is the truth from You, then rain down upon us stones from the sky." [[Its takhrij was previously given in Surah al-Anfal at verse (32).]] ﴿But Allah will never fail His promise.﴾ So He fulfilled that on the Day of Badr (28/a).

﴿And indeed, a day with your Lord is like a thousand years of what you count.﴾ Ibn Kathir, Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read "ya'uddun" (they count) with a ya' here, because of His saying: ﴿And they ask you to hasten﴾. The rest read it with a ta', because it is more general, since it is addressed to those who hasten and to the believers. They agreed on the ta' in Tanzil al-Sajdah (the Surah of As-Sajdah).

Ibn ʿAbbas said: It means one of the six days in which Allah created the heavens and the earth.

Mujahid and Ikrimah said: It means one of the days of the Hereafter. The evidence for this is what was narrated from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Rejoice, O assembly of destitute emigrants, in perfect light on the Day of Resurrection: you will enter Paradise half a day before the rich among the people, and that is the measure of five hundred years."[[Abu Dawud related it in al-ʿIlm, chapter on stories (5/255–256). Al-Mundhiri said in its isnad there is al-Mu'alla ibn Ziyad, and there is some discussion concerning him. Then he cited a corroborating report from Abu Hurairah, related by al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah. Also Imam Ahmad (3/63), and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah (14/191–192).]]

Ibn Zayd said: "And indeed, a day with your Lord is like a thousand years of what you count" refers to the days of the Hereafter. And His saying: ﴿whose measure is fifty thousand years of what you count﴾ refers to the Day of Resurrection. The meaning according to this is: they hasten the punishment, while a single day of their punishment in the Hereafter is a thousand years.

It was also said: The meaning is that a day of the punishment they have hastened, in its heaviness, its prolongation and its severity, is like a thousand years of what you count, so how can you hasten it? This is like the saying: "The days of worry are long, and the days of joy are short."

It was also said: The meaning is that a day with Him and a thousand years in respite are equal, because He is capable: whenever He wills, He seizes them, and nothing escapes Him through delay. Thus His power to bring about the punishment they are hastening and His delaying it are equal. This is the meaning of the saying of Ibn ʿAbbas in the narration of ʿAtaʾ.
