Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 22, verse 52:

His statement, may He be exalted and glorified: ﴿Never did We send before you any messenger or prophet but that when he had a desire, Satan threw [something] into his desire﴾, to the end of the verse. Ibn 'Abbas, Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi and others among the exegetes (mufassirun) said: When the Messenger of God ﷺ saw his people turning away from him, and was grieved by how far they kept from what had come to them from God, he wished within himself that something would come to him from God that would bring him and his people closer together, out of his eagerness for their faith. One day he was in a gathering of Quraysh, and God sent down the surah "al-Najm" (The Star). The Messenger of God ﷺ recited it until he reached His words: ﴿Have you considered al-Lat, al-'Uzza, and Manat, the third, the other?﴾ Satan cast upon his tongue, from what he had been speaking to himself and desiring: "Those are the exalted cranes, and their intercession is indeed to be hoped for." When Quraysh heard that, they rejoiced at it. The Messenger of God ﷺ continued his recitation, reciting the whole surah, and he prostrated at the end of the surah. The Muslims prostrated with his prostration, and all those in the mosque among the polytheists prostrated too. No one remained in the mosque, believer or unbeliever, who did not prostrate, except al-Walid ibn al-Mughira and Abu Uhayha Sa'id ibn al-'As. They each took a handful of gravel from the valley (al-Batha') and raised it to their foreheads and prostrated upon it, because they were two elderly men who could not manage the prostration. Quraysh dispersed, pleased with what they had heard of the mention of their gods, and they said: "Muhammad has mentioned our gods in the best of mentions." And they said: "We know that God gives life and causes death, creates and provides, but these gods of ours intercede for us with Him, so if he has granted them a share, we are with him." When the Messenger of God ﷺ reached evening, Jibril came to him and said: "O Muhammad, what have you done? You have recited to the people what I did not bring you from God, may He be mighty and majestic!" The Messenger of God ﷺ was greatly saddened and feared God with a great fear, so God sent down this verse to console him, and He was merciful to him. The Companions of the Prophet ﷺ who were in the land of Abyssinia heard of this and learned of Quraysh's prostration. It is also said: Quraysh and the people of Makkah had embraced Islam, and most of them returned to their clans, saying: "They are dearer to us." But when they approached Makkah, they learned that what they had been told about the Islam of the people of Makkah was false, so no one entered except under protection or in secret. When this verse was revealed, Quraysh said: "Muhammad has regretted what he mentioned of the standing of our gods with God, so he has changed that." The two phrases that Satan had cast upon the tongue of the Messenger of God ﷺ had settled in the mouth of every polytheist, so they increased in evil beyond what they were already in, and in severity against whoever had embraced Islam.

God, may He be exalted, said: ﴿Never did We send before you any messenger﴾, meaning one to whom Jibril brings the revelation openly, ﴿nor any prophet﴾, meaning one whose prophethood is by inspiration or in a dream. Every messenger is a prophet, but not every prophet is a messenger. ﴿But when he had a desire﴾. Some of them said: that is, he loved something and longed for it, and spoke to himself about what he had not been commanded.

﴿Satan threw [something] into his desire﴾, that is, into what he intended.

And it is reported from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: When he spoke, Satan cast into his speech and found a way to it. No prophet has ever desired that his people believe in him without Satan casting upon him what would please his people, and God then abrogates what Satan has cast.

Most of the exegetes said: The meaning of His words ﴿tamanna﴾ (desired) is: he recited and read the Book of God, may He be exalted. ﴿Satan threw into his desire﴾, that is, into his recitation. The poet said about 'Uthman when he was killed: "He recited the Book of God at the first night / and at its last met the death-fate of destinies." (Here tamanna is used in the sense of reciting, so the Arabic word tamanna, "to desire," is explained as "to recite.")

They differed over whether he was reciting during the prayer or outside the prayer. Some people said: he was reciting during the prayer. Others said: he was reciting outside the prayer. If it is asked: how is error in recitation permissible for the Prophet ﷺ, when he was protected from error in the foundations of the religion, and when God, mighty is His remembrance, said in the Qur'an: ﴿Falsehood cannot approach it from before it or from behind it﴾ (Fussilat 41:42), meaning Iblis?

It is answered: People have differed in responding to this. Some of them said: the Messenger ﷺ did not recite it, but Satan uttered that between his recitations, so the polytheists thought that the Messenger had recited it.

Qatada said: The Prophet ﷺ dozed off briefly, and that flowed upon his tongue through Satan's casting, and he had no awareness of it.

Most of them said: That flowed upon his tongue through Satan's casting, by way of inadvertence and forgetfulness, and God soon alerted him to it.

It is also said: A devil called Abyad (the White) did this deed, and that was a trial and a test from God, mighty and majestic, by which He tests His servants as He wills.

[[That this story, known as the story of the Gharaniq (the cranes), has been mentioned by most of the exegetes without comment. Al-Tabari mentioned it (17/186–190), and Ibn Kathir in his tafsir (3/230–231), then said: "Muhammad ibn Ishaq mentioned it in the Sira with something like this, all of it as mursal and munqati' reports (with broken chains). And Allah knows best." Whoever traces the routes of this story finds that all its routes are mursal, munqati', mu'all (defective), or contain unknown narrators (jahala). **Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 22, verses 59–63:**

﴿He will certainly admit them to an entrance with which they will be pleased﴾ because in it they will have what their souls desire and what their eyes delight in. ﴿And indeed, Allah is All-Knowing﴾ of their intentions, ﴿Forbearing﴾ toward them.

﴿That﴾ means: the matter is that which We have related to you. ﴿And whoever retaliates with the like of what he was punished with﴾ means he repays the wrongdoer with the like of his wrong. Al-Hasan said: this means he fights the polytheists as they fought him. ﴿Then he is wronged﴾ means he is wronged by being driven out of his home. That is, what the polytheists inflicted upon the Muslims by way of oppression, to the point that they compelled them to leave their homelands. It was revealed concerning a group of polytheists who came upon a group of Muslims during the last two nights of al-Muharram (the first month of the Islamic calendar). The Muslims disliked fighting them and asked them to refrain from fighting for the sake of the sacred month (al-shahr al-haram). The polytheists refused and fought them. That is their oppression against them. The Muslims stood firm against them and were given victory over them. The first "punishment" (in the verse) carries the meaning of recompense. ﴿Indeed, Allah is Pardoning and Forgiving﴾: He pardons the faults of the believers and forgives their sins.

﴿That﴾ means: that victory, ﴿because Allah﴾, who is Capable of whatever He wills. From His power is that: ﴿He causes the night to enter into the day and causes the day to enter into the night, and Allah is Hearing and Seeing﴾. ﴿That is because Allah is the Truth, and that which they invoke besides Him is falsehood﴾. The people of Basrah, Hamzah, al-Kisa'i and Hafs read it with the ya' (yaduna, "they invoke", third person), while the others read it with the ta' (tad'una, "you invoke"), meaning the polytheists. ﴿And indeed, Allah is the Most High﴾ above everything, ﴿the Great﴾, the Magnificent, before whom everything is insignificant.

﴿Have you not seen that Allah sends down water from the sky, and the earth becomes green﴾ with vegetation? ﴿Indeed, Allah is Subtle﴾ with the provision of His servants and in bringing forth vegetation from the earth, ﴿Acquainted﴾ with what is in the hearts of the servants and with bringing forth vegetation from the earth when the rain is delayed from them.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 22, verses 64–67:

﴿To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth﴾: as slaves and as dominion. ﴿And indeed, Allah is the Free of need﴾ from His servants, ﴿the Praiseworthy﴾ in His actions.

﴿Have you not seen that Allah has subjected to you whatever is on the earth and the ships﴾, meaning: and He subjected to you the ships, ﴿sailing through the sea by His command﴾. It was also said: "whatever is on the earth" refers to the animals that are ridden on land, and "the ships" are ridden on the sea. ﴿And He holds back the sky from falling upon the earth﴾, meaning: lest it fall upon the earth, ﴿except by His permission. Indeed, Allah is Kind and Merciful to the people﴾. ﴿And it is He who gave you life﴾, meaning: He brought you into being when you were nothing; ﴿then He causes you to die﴾ when your terms are fulfilled; ﴿then He will bring you to life﴾ on the Day of Resurrection for reward and punishment. ﴿Indeed, mankind is ungrateful﴾ for the blessings of Allah.

The saying of the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿For every nation We have appointed a rite (mansak) which they perform﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: it means a law (shari'ah) which they act upon. It is narrated from him that he said: "a festival (ʿīd)." Qatadah and Mujahid said: a place of sacrifice where they slaughter. It was also said: a place of worship. And it was said: a familiar place which they frequent.

In the language of the Arabs, the mansak (مَنْسَك, place of ritual) is the customary place for doing good or evil, and from it comes "manasik al-hajj" (the rites of Hajj), because people repeatedly go to the places where the acts of Hajj are performed.

﴿So let them not dispute with you concerning the matter﴾, meaning concerning the matter of slaughtering animals. It was revealed concerning Budayl ibn Warqa', Bishr ibn Sufyan, and Yazid ibn Khunays, who said to the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ): "What is the matter with you that you eat what you kill with your own hands, but do not eat what Allah has killed?" [[See: al-Qurtubi: 12/93.]]

Al-Zajjaj said: the meaning of His saying ﴿So let them not dispute with you﴾ is: do not dispute with them yourself, as one says, "So-and-so does not quarrel with you," meaning, "do not quarrel with him." This is permissible in what occurs between two parties, but it is not permissible to say, "So-and-so does not strike you," meaning, "do not strike him," because disputing and quarrelling are not complete except between two, so if one of them is left out, there is no quarrel there.

﴿And invite to your Lord﴾: to belief in your Lord, ﴿indeed you are upon a straight guidance﴾.

﴿To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth﴾: as slaves and as dominion. ﴿And indeed, Allah is the Free of need﴾ from His servants, ﴿the Praiseworthy﴾ in His actions.

﴿Have you not seen that Allah has subjected to you whatever is on the earth and the ships﴾, meaning: and He subjected to you the ships, ﴿sailing through the sea by His command﴾. It was also said: "whatever is on the earth" refers to the animals that are ridden on land, and "the ships" are ridden on the sea. ﴿And He holds back the sky from falling upon the earth﴾, meaning: lest it fall upon the earth, ﴿except by His permission. Indeed, Allah is Kind and Merciful to the people﴾. ﴿And it is He who gave you life﴾, meaning: He brought you into being when you were nothing; ﴿then He causes you to die﴾ when your terms are fulfilled; ﴿then He will bring you to life﴾ on the Day of Resurrection for reward and punishment. ﴿Indeed, mankind is ungrateful﴾ for the blessings of Allah.

It is narrated from him that he said: "a festival (ʿīd)." Qatadah and Mujahid said: a place of sacrifice where they slaughter. It was also said: a place of worship. And it was said: a familiar place which they frequent.

In the language of the Arabs, the mansak (مَنْسَك, place of ritual) is the customary place for doing good or evil, and from it comes "manasik al-hajj" (the rites of Hajj), because people repeatedly go to the places where the acts of Hajj are performed.

﴿And invite to your Lord﴾: to belief in your Lord, ﴿indeed you are upon a straight guidance﴾.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 22, verses 68–72:

﴿And if they dispute with you, say: "Allah knows best what you do."﴾

﴿O mankind, a parable is presented, so listen to it.﴾ The meaning of "ḍuriba" (was presented): "juʿila" (was made), as in their saying: "ḍaraba al-sulṭān al-baʿtha ʿalā al-nās" (the ruler imposed the levy upon the people), and "ḍaraba al-jizya ʿalā ahl al-dhimma" (he imposed the poll-tax upon the protected people), meaning he made that obligatory upon them. The meaning of ﴿so listen to it﴾ is: so listen to its state and its description. Then He explained that, saying:

﴿Indeed, those you invoke besides Allah﴾ means: the idols. Yaʿqub recited it with the yāʾ (yaʿ-lamūn form, "yadʿūna"), and the rest recited it with the tāʾ (tadʿūna). ﴿will never create a fly﴾, one, even in its smallness and insignificance, because they have no power over it. "Al-dhubāb" (fly) is singular; its paucal plural is "adhibba" and its plural of abundance is "dhibbān," like "ghurāb" (crow) with "aghriba" and "ghirbān." ﴿Even if they gathered together for it﴾, that is, to create it. ﴿And if the fly should snatch away from them anything, they could not retrieve it from it.﴾ Ibn ʿAbbas said: they used to smear the idols with saffron, and when it dried the fly came and snatched from it.

It was also said the reverse: "the seeker" is the idol and "the sought" is the fly. Al-Ḍaḥḥak said: "the seeker" is the worshipper and "the sought" is the worshipped.

﴿They have not measured Allah with His true measure.﴾ They did not magnify Him with His true magnificence, nor did they know Him with His true knowledge, nor did they describe Him with His true description, when they associated with Him what cannot defend itself from the fly nor take vengeance upon it. ﴿Indeed, Allah is Strong, Mighty.﴾

﴿Allah chooses﴾, that is, selects, ﴿from among the angels messengers﴾, and they are Jibril, Mika'il, Israfil, ʿAzrail and others; ﴿and from among mankind﴾, that is, He selects from among mankind messengers such as Ibrahim, Musa, ʿIsa, Muhammad (ﷺ) and others of the prophets, peace be upon them. It was revealed when the polytheists said: "Has the Reminder been sent down to him from among us?" So He informed them that the choosing is up to Him; He chooses whom He wills of His creation. [[See: al-Qurtubi: 12/98.]]

﴿Indeed, Allah is All-Hearing, All-Seeing.﴾ That is, He hears their saying and sees whom He chooses for His message.

The scholars differed about the prostration of recitation (sujud al-tilawa, the prostration performed upon reciting a verse of prostration) at the recitation of this verse.

A group held that one prostrates at it. This is the view of 'Umar, 'Ali, Ibn 'Umar, Ibn Mas'ud and Ibn 'Abbas, and Ibn al-Mubarak, al-Shafi'i, Ahmad and Ishaq also said so. The commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 22, verse 78:

His words, exalted is He: ﴿And strive for Allah with the striving due to Him﴾. It was said: strive in the way of Allah against the enemies of Allah. "The striving due to Him" is exerting one's full capacity in it. This was said by Ibn 'Abbas. And from him also, he said: "Do not fear the blame of any blamer in Allah's cause," for that is the striving due to Him, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿They strive in the way of Allah and do not fear the blame of any blamer﴾ (al-Ma'idah: 54).

Al-Dahhak and Muqatil said: act for Allah with the action due to Him, and worship Him with the worship due to Him.

Muqatil ibn Sulayman said: it was abrogated (naskh) by His saying [[See what has preceded: 3/2, note (1).]] ﴿So fear Allah as much as you are able﴾ (al-Taghabun: 16). Most of the exegetes said: "the striving due to Him" is that one's intention be sincere and truthful for Allah, exalted is He. Al-Suddi said: it is that He be obeyed and not disobeyed.

'Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak said: it is the striving against the self and its desires, and this is the greater striving (al-jihad al-akbar), and this is the striving due to Him. It has been related that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), when he returned from the Battle of Tabuk, said: "We have returned from the lesser striving (al-jihad al-asghar) to the greater striving (al-jihad al-akbar)." [[Ibn Hajar said in al-Kafi al-Shafi, p. 114: "Al-Tha'labi mentioned it without a chain, and al-Bayhaqi narrated it in al-Zuhd from the hadith of Jabir, who said: A group of raiders came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he said: 'You have come with the best arrival from the lesser striving to the greater striving.' It was said: 'And what is the greater striving?' He said: 'The servant's striving against his desire.'" He said: "In it there is weakness." I (Ibn Hajar) say: it is from the narration of 'Isa ibn Ibrahim from Yahya ibn Ya'la from Layth ibn Abi Sulaym, and the three are weak. Al-Nasa'i mentioned it in al-Kuna as a saying of Ibrahim ibn Abi 'Ablah, one of the Successors (tabi'un) from the people of Syria. Al-Khatib al-Baghdadi narrated it in al-Tarikh: 13/493, and al-Iraqi, in Takhrij Ahadith al-Ihya': 3/7, attributed it to al-Bayhaqi and said: "This chain has weakness." See Kashf al-Khafa': 1/511; Da'if al-Jami' al-Saghir: 14/118; al-Asrar al-Marfu'a fi al-Ahadith al-Mawdu'a by al-Qari, pp. 211–212.]] By "the lesser striving" he meant striving against the disbelievers, and by "the greater striving" he meant striving against the self.

﴿He has chosen you﴾, that is, He has selected you for His religion. ﴿And He has not placed upon you in the religion any hardship (haraj)﴾, that is, narrowness. Its meaning is that the believer is not afflicted with any sin except that Allah makes for him a way out of it: for some sins, by repentance; for some, by restoring wrongful takings and retaliation; and for some, by various kinds of expiations (kaffarat). So there is no sin in the religion of Islam for which the servant does not find a path to deliverance from punishment.

It was also said: [the hardship is] narrowness in the times of your obligations, such as the crescent of the month of Ramadan, the breaking of the fast (al-fitr), and the time of the Hajj, when these become unclear to you; He has made it broad for you until you are certain.

Muqatil said: it means the concessions (rukhas) at times of necessity, such as shortening the prayer during travel, tayammum, eating carrion in cases of necessity, breaking the fast due to travel or illness, and praying while seated when unable. This is also the view of al-Kalbi.

It has been related from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: the hardship was the heavy burdens (al-asal) that were upon the Children of Israel; Allah removed them from this community. [[Al-Suyuti attributed it in al-Durr al-Manthur: 6/78 to Ibn Abi Hatim with the wording: "The burden (al-isr) that was upon the Children of Israel has been removed from you."]]

﴿The religion of your father Ibrahim﴾: that is, the word (kalimah) of your father; it is in the accusative by the removal of the preposition of description (harf al-sifah). It was also said: it is in the accusative by way of incitement (al-ighra'), meaning: follow the religion of your father Ibrahim. [And He commanded us to follow the religion of Ibrahim] [[What is between the brackets is omitted from "b".]] because it is included within the religion of Muhammad (ﷺ).

If it is said: what is the sense of His saying ﴿the religion of your father﴾, when not all Muslims trace their lineage to Ibrahim?

It is said: He addressed the Arabs with it, and they were of the offspring of Ibrahim. It was also said: He addressed with it all the Muslims, and Ibrahim is a father to them, in the sense of the obligation to honor him and preserve his right, just as a father is to be honored. This is like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And his wives are their mothers﴾ (al-Ahzab: 6). And the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "I am to you only like a father [to his child]" [[A part of a hadith narrated by Abu Dawud in al-Taharah, chapter: The disliking of facing the qibla when relieving oneself: 1/18, with the wording: "I am to you only in the position of a father," and by al-Nasa'i in al-Taharah, chapter: The prohibition of cleaning with dung: 1/38, and by Ibn Majah in al-Taharah, chapter: Istinja' with stones and the prohibition of dung and bones: 1/114, no. (313), and by al-Darimi 1/172–173, and Ibn Hibban authenticated it, no. (128), p. (62), and Ibn Khuzaymah 1/44, and al-Shafi'i 1/28, and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah 1/356, where he said: this is a sound hadith.]] [[Addition from "b".]].

﴿He named you﴾: meaning that Allah, exalted is He, named you ﴿the Muslims﴾ ﴿from before﴾, meaning from before the revelation of the Qur'an, in the earlier Books.

﴿And in this﴾: that is, in the Book. This is the view of most of the exegetes. Ibn Zayd said: "this" refers to Ibrahim, meaning that Ibrahim named you Muslims in his time, before this time and in this time, and that is his saying: ﴿Our Lord, make us Muslims to You, and of our descendants a Muslim nation to You﴾ (al-Baqarah: 127). ﴿That the Messenger may be a witness over you﴾ on the Day of Resurrection that he has conveyed to you, ﴿and that you may be witnesses over the people﴾ that their messengers have conveyed to them. ﴿So establish prayer, give zakah, and hold fast to Allah﴾, that is: trust in Allah and rely upon Him. Al-Hasan said: hold fast to the religion of Allah. It has been related from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: ask your Lord to protect you from everything you dislike. [[See Zad al-Masir 5/457.]] It was also said: its meaning is: call upon Him that He may make you firm in His religion. It was also said: holding fast to Allah is adherence to the Book and the Sunnah. ﴿He is your Protector (mawla)﴾ [and your Helper (waliyyukum)] [[Omitted from "b".]] and your Supporter and your Guardian, ﴿so excellent is the Protector and excellent is the Helper﴾, the Helper for you.
